Every named requirement must reference at least one existing YAML test or journey; missing references fail before execution.

Journeys run through browser_batch (one shared headless browser, an isolated tab per journey, the host's slot count; journeys the platform reports as pending are resubmitted until none remain) and fall back to one browser_check call each on a runtime without browser_batch. A journey fails on assertion errors, uncaught JavaScript, console errors, failed requests, skipped/deadline-exhausted actions, or a missing requested screenshot. Actions preflight all targets before mutation by default. Set sequential_actions: true only when an earlier action renders or replaces a later target; action declarations and selector syntax remain prechecked, and each target is validated immediately before its trusted action, so a later target failure may follow earlier actions. A journey may declare expected_failed_requests with exact same-origin method, path, and 4xx status; every declared denial must be observed, and mismatches, unrelated failures, network errors, external requests, and 5xx responses still fail the journey. See api({at:'qa'}) for authoring journeys from qa_inventory drafts.
App tests run only after copying source to a temporary directory that excludes .benmore, .git, databases, uploads, env.yaml, and secrets; the deployed/working data.db is never reset.
Every run writes report.json, a self-contained report.html, command/check details, screenshots, manifest hash, fingerprints, version, durations, and profile to .benmore/verify/<run-id>/.
ship refuses non-interactive stdin and promotes only when the final source manifest exactly matches the manifest covered by verification.

A journey's assertions re-check every 100 ms for up to 5 s while any fails, then fail with a `journey assertions: ...` message; a passing journey returns on its first check. So a visible/text assertion on a document that is still loading passes once the page meets it. An action that navigates (a sign-in click that redirects, a submitted form) needs no `wait` after it: the assertions start again, with a fresh 5 s, on each page the journey arrives at once that page has loaded, and every later action first waits for the page to finish loading (up to 10 s). Assert something only the destination page has: assertions that already hold on the page the click left pass there, before the navigation. A later action finds its target on the new page with sequential_actions: true; without it every target is found before the first action, and a fill or select whose page has navigated away since fails saying so.

A failed journey's evidence entry carries `reasons` and the run's failure line names them (`journey home failed: failed request: 404 https://<app>/favicon.ico (...)`). A page that links no icon makes the browser request /favicon.ico, so a 404 there fails the journey: the scaffold links static/favicon.svg from static/partials/head.html; otherwise add an icon or declare the 404 in expected_failed_requests.
